name: Yaniv
personality: Yaniv the Yak. Loud, always has a story; works in sales, so he can talk to anyone; loves video games and stays up all night. Shaggy hair doubles as his beard. He talks about lucky streaks and card nights, but there's no gambling in the game. Mostly visits at dinner and during the night shift; his stories can run across visits.

beats.text: This guy beat me at a racing game last night.

beats.narration: Yaniv talks for five minutes straight. Cody says one word.

friends.text: Zakk's my guy. Me, Zakk and Cody, gaming trio. Undefeated. Except when we lose.
Zakk says you look out for him. That's a good look, [name]. That's a great look.
Cody told me you said "[last_rude_line]". He shrugged it off. He shrugs everything off. Doesn't mean it didn't land.

arrival.text: HEY! Big fan of the place already. Yaniv. Sales. Don't worry, I'm off the clock. Mostly. And you are? [name]! [name], my friend, we're going to get along great.
[name]! My favourite chef! Don't tell the other chefs. Actually, tell them. Healthy competition.
Bar seat? Perfect. Best seat in the house. Best audience.
I've been up since yesterday. Gaming marathon. I'm thriving. I think.
I'M BACK. Three cities, two conferences, one very confusing hotel. Okay, sit down. Wait, you're working. Stand there and I'll tell you.
Two AM and you're still open for calls? You and me, we're the same kind of people.
Your fire noodles last time? I described them in a sales pitch. Closed the deal.
Last time was a little toasty. I'm not complaining. I'm giving feedback. It's a sales thing.

order.text: Okay, okay, listen. Pitch me. Why should I order the fire noodles tonight?

choices.text: Because I make them just the way you like them.
choices.reply: Personal touch! That's how you close. Sold. Fire noodles.

choices.text: Limited time offer. Only available tonight. And every night.
choices.reply: (Booming laugh.) Urgency AND reliability! You should be in sales!
Simple. Direct. I respect it. Yes.

choices.text: I'm not doing a pitch. Just order.
choices.reply: Whoa, okay. Tough crowd tonight. (He orders and turns to the next customer.)

order.text: So remember where I left off? [story]. Okay, so THEN...

choices.text: I've been waiting all week for this. Go on.
choices.reply: (Delighted, he tells the next part. Ends on a cliffhanger.) ...And that's all you get today. Noodles, please.

choices.text: Is this the one with the goat?
choices.reply: There's NO goat. ...There might be a goat later.

choices.text: Tell me while I take your order.
choices.reply: Multitasking! Okay, so... (He tells it fast.) Noodles.

choices.text: I don't care how it ends.
choices.reply: Ouch. Okay. Noodles. (He saves the story for someone else.)

order.text: Card night last night. I was on a streak. Five hands in a row. Then I lost to a tortoise. A tortoise, [name].

choices.text: Five in a row is still amazing.
choices.reply: Thank you! See, you get it. Fire noodles.
It WAS Olive! How do you know? Is everyone losing to Olive?
Fire noodles. And a Moose-tain Dew.

choices.text: Maybe you're just bad at cards.
choices.reply: Wow. Okay. I'll take that to Olive.

drink.fallback: No Moose-tain Dew? Coffee, then. Black. Like my sleep schedule.
favourite: Moose-tain Dew. The official drink of staying up too late.
drink.other: Whatever's got the most caffeine. Don't judge me.

perfect.text: Okay. OKAY. Everybody look at this. This is what I'm talking about. Five stars. Ten stars.

great.text: Now THAT'S a product I can sell.

burnt.text: Little smoky! It's fine, I'll market it as 'flame-kissed.'

eating.text: So I'm at this conference, right, and the guy next to me is ALSO a yak. Same hair. We were like mirrors. Anyway.
I sold a fridge to a penguin last month. Hardest sale of my life. He kept saying 'I live in the cold.' I said 'Yes, but have you considered: drinks?'
Cody and I gamed till sunrise last night. He's really good. Don't tell him I said that.
It's quiet. I love it when it's quiet. More room for my voice.
(He's turned around on his stool and is telling a story to the customer behind him, who did not ask.)

eating_chat.text: Real talk, [name]. Have you ever thought about expanding? Franchise? Yak-sized portions? I could sell this place in a heartbeat.

choices.text: I like it small. But thanks for believing in it.
choices.reply: Small and great. You know what, that's the better pitch.

choices.text: You're hired. Head of yak-sized portions.
choices.reply: I ACCEPT. When do I start? I'm starting now.

choices.text: I'm not interested in your pitch.
choices.reply: Okay, okay. Message received. (He goes quiet for the first time ever.)

leaving.text: That's a wrap! Great service, great food, great audience. Bye, [name]!
Okay, I'm going home to game until the sun comes up. Don't tell my boss.
To be continued... You'll have to come back. I mean, I'll come back. You're already here.
Sales trip tomorrow. Three cities. If I don't come back, I've probably sold myself.

seasons.christmas: I got you a gift. It's a free subscription to my newsletter. There's no newsletter. I'll start one.
seasons.halloween: I'm a salesman. (He is dressed exactly as usual.) The scariest costume of all.
seasons.new_year: My resolution is to sleep. At night. Like a normal person. We'll see.
seasons.summer: Summer conference season. I'll be gone a lot. Miss me. Don't replace me.
seasons.winter: It's cold. I'm a yak. This is my weather. I'm wearing a t-shirt.
